title: Technology Sector Update for 05/09/2018: MB,MTCH,WB

Technology stocks were sharply higher on Wednesday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding almost 0.9% in value while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 1.0% gain.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- MindBody ( MB ) plunged 20% on Wednesday after the cloud-based business management software firm issued Q2 and FY18 revenue guidance missing Wall Street expectations. The company is expecting revenue during the current quarter ending June 30 in a range of $59.5 million to $61.5 million, trailing the Capital IQ consensus by at least $1.1 million. It also sees FY18 revenue of between $246 million to $252 million compared with the analyst mean looking for $254.6 million in revenue for the 12 months ending Dec. 31. The weak forecast upstaged above-consensus Q1 earnings, with MindBody company late Tuesday reporting net income of $0.06 per share during the three months ended March 31, reversing a $0.03 per share net loss during the same quarter last year and topping the Street view by $0.02 per share. Revenue grew 28% year over year to $53.8 million from $42.2 million last year and matching the $53.84 million consensus call.
In other sector news:
+ Match Group ( MTCH ) was edging back on to positive ground on Wednesday, bouncing back from a nearly 8% decline earlier in the session and retracing much of a small gain that followed the online dating company reporting Q1 financial results beating Wall Street forecasts. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.26 per share during the three months ended March 31, topping the Capital IQ consensus expecting $0.24 per share. Net sales rose 36% over the same quarter last year to $407 million, also exceeding the Street view by around $22.2 million.
- Weibo Corp ( WB ) stumbled Wednesday, at one point falling almost 15%, despite the Chinese social media company exceeding analyst projections with Q1 financal results. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.50 per American depositary share, almost doubling its $0.26 per ADS profit during the first three months in 2017 and topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.03 per ADS. Total revenue rose to $349.9 million during the January-to-March reporting period from $199.2 million during the same quarter last year and beating the $343.9 million analyst mean. For the current quarter, Weibo is expecting revenue between $420 million and $430 million, straddling the $423.9 million Street view.
